parts.title: PART I — PERSONS, NAMES AND STATUS

sections.title: Section 1. The Designation of Every Person
rules: Rule 001. Every person shall possess 1819 complete names, one appointed to each 1819th of the day. The names shall be used only during their appointed 1819th and shall not share an initial letter. Failure to use the correct name shall require the person to introduce themselves by all 1819 names, in order, on every occasion for the next 1819 days.

Rule 002. Each person shall observe 1819 birthdays in every year: the actual anniversary of their birth and the date exactly 0.01819 multiplied by the birthday it is days after it. On each one shall give the SR 1819SRs (standard reference—£1819)

Rule 003. Every person shall state their age in years, months, days, hours and seconds and divisions of the SR (Standard Reference—0.01819 microsecs) whenever their age is requested. The figures shall be calculated from the time of birth to the nearest microsecond, not from the beginning of the date.
Rule 004. No person shall sign the same signature on 1819 consecutive dates. Each signature shall remain recognisably theirs while differing in the shape, order or form of at least three letters.
Rule 005. Every person shall learn to write their full name in 19 scripts, including 18 no longer used for ordinary communication. The name shall be written 1819 times in each script every day.

Rule 006. A person whose name contains fewer than 1819 letters shall append a chosen word to it for formal declarations. The chosen word shall contain exactly 1819 letters and shall be changed every 1819th of a year.
Rule 007. Every person shall measure the length of their own shadow at noon on both solstices and both equinoxes. The four measurements shall be stated in SRs and compared before the end of the year.

Rule 008. No person shall claim to have been born on a particular date without also being able to state the day of the week, the hour, the minute, the second, microsecond, nanosecond and SR. Where the hour or minute is unknown, the person shall provide a written explanation of no fewer than 18,191,819 hundred words.

parts.title: PART II — SPEECH, LANGUAGE AND WRITTEN EXPRESSION

sections.title: Section 2. The Use of Words
rules: Rule 009. Every person shall speak only in sentences containing exactly 1.819 words until noon. Any sentence spoken with a different number shall be repeated correctly 1819 times before another sentence is spoken.
Rule 010. Every public speech exceeding 0.01819 minutes shall contain a passage of no fewer than 18,191,819 words written in a language that is no longer spoken by any nation.
Rule 011. No person shall use the same adjective twice in one public address. A repeated adjective shall require the entire address to be delivered again 1819 times, with the repetitions removed.

Rule 012. Every person shall learn the alphabet of 1819 languages or, where fewer languages are documented, every documented alphabet and writing system, and shall recite each backwards 1819 times each 1819th of a SR (for time—1819th of a nanosecond). Each recitation shall be completed without reference to a written copy. The order of languages shall be reversed at every repetition.

Rule 013. No written work exceeding 0.1819 thousand words shall contain the same first word in two consecutive paragraphs. Where the repetition occurs, the second paragraph shall be rewritten in full 1819 more times.

Rule 014. Every letter, piece of text or email sent on the final day of a month shall contain a sentence of exactly 1819 words. The sentence shall be neither the first nor the last sentence of the letter.
Rule 015. No person shall answer a question with a single word on a Sunday. The answer shall contain at least 18,191,819 words and shall address the question directly.
Rule 016. Every person shall refrain from using anything containing or related to anything containing the letters ‘S’ and ‘R’ for the entire month of November.

title: BOOK II — TIME AND THE HEAVENS

parts.title: PART III — THE CALENDAR AND THE PASSAGE OF TIME

sections.title: Section 3. The Division of Days
rules: Rule 017. Every year shall contain a 1819th month after the twelfth, lasting 1819 days. No ordinary appointment, payment or undertaking shall be transferred out of that month on the ground that it is absent from other calendars.

Rule 018. The final minute of every hour shall be counted backwards, beginning at sixty and ending at one. Any public clock that fails to display this count shall be considered incomplete for that hour.

Rule 019. Every person shall observe the one hundredth day of each year as a second New Year. The observance shall last 1819 consecutive hours, insofar as the calendar permits, and shall include the recitation of the names of all months in reverse order 1819 times. Each recitation shall be followed by the months in forward order 1819 times.
Rule 020. No date shall be written using numerals alone. The day, month and year shall each be written in full words, followed by their numerical form in brackets.
Rule 021. Every person shall remain aware of the exact time at which they were born. On that minute each year, all other activity shall be suspended for a period of sixty seconds.
Rule 022. Every calendar shall display the number of days that have elapsed since the beginning of the current century. The number shall be updated at midnight and shall not be rounded.
Rule 023. No person shall use the expression “for a moment” to describe a period longer than one second. Any longer period shall be stated in seconds, minutes and hours as applicable.

Rule 024. On the last day of every year, every person shall recite all dates of that year in reverse order 1819 times. Each recital shall begin with the final date and end with the first. The entire sequence shall then be recited in forward order 1819 times.

parts.title: PART IV — THE HEAVENS, WEATHER AND CELESTIAL OBSERVANCE

sections.title: Section 4. The Conduct Required by the Sky
rules: Rule 025. Every person shall observe at least one complete sunrise and one complete sunset each month. Each observation shall be made from a different location from the one used in the preceding month.

Rule 026. Whenever an eclipse occurs within the jurisdiction of the SR, every person shall be able to state its beginning, greatest extent and conclusion to the nearest second. A person who cannot observe it directly shall obtain the times from a reliable astronomical source.
Rule 027. Every person shall identify twelve constellations without assistance before their thirtieth birthday. At least four shall be constellations visible only from the opposite hemisphere.
Rule 028. No weather forecast shall state a probability of precipitation without also stating the predicted quantity of rain in millimetres to two decimal places.
Rule 029. Every person who hears thunder for the first time in a calendar year shall write a description of the sound containing no fewer than one hundred and eighty words before the end of that day.
Rule 030. No person shall refer to the moon merely as “the moon” in a formal statement. Its phase, age in days and approximate illuminated fraction shall also be stated.

Rule 031. Every person shall learn the names of the eight planets in order of distance from the Sun and recite them backwards 1819 times on the first day of each season. The names shall then be recited forwards 1819 times, with the recognised dwarf planets included in a separate sequence.

Rule 032. On the longest day of each year, every person shall remain outdoors for one continuous hour between sunrise and sunset, where weather and safety permit. The hour shall be spent facing the direction of the Sun’s apparent movement.

title: BOOK III — TERRITORY AND PUBLIC ORDER

parts.title: PART V — TERRITORY, BOUNDARIES AND GEOGRAPHY

sections.title: Section 5. The Description of the World
rules: Rule 033. Every person shall learn the exact geographical coordinates of their birthplace to six decimal places and shall be able to reproduce them without consulting a map.

Rule 034. Every journey crossing a named boundary shall be preceded by the recitation of the full names of the territories on both sides. The recitation shall take place before the boundary is crossed.
Rule 035. No map shall be considered complete unless it includes a scale in metres, kilometres, miles and degrees of latitude. All four scales shall be shown even where one is unsuitable.

Rule 036. Every person shall visit the geographical centre of the country in which they were born before reaching the age of forty. The centre shall be determined by the calculation of land area, not by population.
Rule 037. No place shall be described as remote without stating its distance from the nearest coastline, the nearest international boundary and the nearest settlement.
Rule 038. Every mountain named on a map shall have its height stated in metres, feet and the number of stair steps that would equal that height. The stair-step figure shall be an estimate.
Rule 039. No person shall describe a journey as crossing a continent unless they can state the names of every country crossed and the total distance travelled within each.
Rule 040. Every island shall be assigned a land-area figure to no fewer than four decimal places. If the island changes size through natural processes, the figure shall be recalculated each year.

parts.title: PART VI — PUBLIC LIFE, LAW AND COLLECTIVE OBLIGATION

sections.title: Section 6. The Conduct of Society
rules: Rule 041. Every person shall attend 1819 public assembly each year that lasts for no fewer than 1819 consecutive hours. The subject of the assembly shall be determined by the Sacred Rulemakers.
Rule 042. No public declaration shall be considered complete until it has been read aloud three times: once at ordinary speed, once at half speed and once at twice ordinary speed.

Rule 043. Every person shall submit one proposed law to the Sacred Rulemakers each year. The proposal shall contain no fewer than one thousand words and shall concern a matter not previously addressed by the proposer.

Rule 044. No agreement containing more than thirteen clauses shall be signed until every clause has been read aloud by every person who is to be bound by it. The reading shall be repeated if any clause is omitted.
Rule 045. Every public holiday shall last for exactly twenty-seven hours. Its beginning and end shall be stated in local time and in Coordinated Universal Time.

Rule 046. No public building shall be opened for the first time without a ceremony lasting at least one hour for every floor above ground level. The ceremony shall take place before the building is used.

Rule 047. Every person shall memorise the first and final sentence of every law that directly governs their occupation, residence or principal activity. Each sentence shall be recited 1819 times on the first day of each year, first forwards and then backwards, word by word.

Rule 048. No dispute shall be declared settled until each side has stated the other side’s position to that side’s satisfaction. The statement shall be made without shortening or paraphrasing the principal claims.

title: BOOK IV — WEALTH, KNOWLEDGE AND OCCUPATION

parts.title: PART VII — MONEY, PROPERTY AND COMMERCE

sections.title: Section 7. The Exchange and Keeping of Wealth
rules: Rule 049. Every person shall retain the first coin or banknote received in each currency they use. It shall remain in their possession until a second payment in that currency has been received, after which it may be spent.
Rule 050. No price shall be stated as a whole number. Every price shall include at least 1819 digits after the decimal point, even where the additional digits are zero.

Rule 051. Every person who completes a purchase shall calculate the price again in a 1819 different currencies before leaving the place of purchase. The second calculation shall use the exchange rate published in that nanosecond.

Rule 052. No object shall be inherited without its new owner learning the names of at least 1819 previous owners, where those names can be established. If fewer than 1819 owners existed, the known history shall be recited 1819 times.

Rule 053. Every contract shall state its duration in days, hours and minutes, as well as seconds, micro nano seconds and SRs. A duration stated only in years or months shall have no force until converted into those units.
Rule 054. No person shall sell an object for an amount ending in the same three digits as the year in which it was made. If the year is unknown, the amount shall end in three zeros.
Rule 055. Every person shall keep 1819 units of currency from a country they have never visited. It shall not be exchanged, spent or given away during that person’s lifetime.
Rule 056. No commercial transaction shall be completed without the total being stated in words, numerals and Roman numerals. All three forms shall represent the same amount.

parts.title: PART VIII — EDUCATION, SCIENCE AND OCCUPATION

sections.title: Section 8. The Required Pursuit of Knowledge
rules: Rule 057. Every person shall study  the Standard Rulebook for 1819 uninterrupted hours on each day.

Rule 058. Every examination shall include 1819 question requiring an answer of exactly one 1819 words and 1819 question requiring an answer of exactly 1.819 word. Neither question shall be identified in advance.
Rule 059. No published scientific result shall be accepted as complete until the experiment has been repeated on 1819 different cities, under 1819 different phases of the moon.
Rule 060. Every person shall count to 1819181918191819 in a language other than their first language every day.

Rule 061. Every book used for formal instruction shall contain a chapter devoted entirely to a subject that is not mentioned elsewhere in the book. The chapter shall be no shorter than 1819 pages. (SR excepted)

Rule 062. No person shall use a mathematical result in a public calculation without being able to provide 1819 alternative methods of reaching the same result. The other methods shall not repeat the first method’s principal steps.

Rule 063. Every person shall complete one course of study in a field wholly unrelated to their occupation before their 0.1819th birthday. The course shall include an examination set by the Sacred Rulemakers.
Rule 064. Every invention shall be accompanied by a description of its operation written from the perspective of the invention itself. The description shall contain no fewer than five hundred words.

title: BOOK V — MOVEMENT AND THE NATURAL WORLD

parts.title: PART IX — TRAVEL, BUILDINGS AND TRANSPORT

sections.title: Section 9. The Movement of Persons and Things
rules: Rule 065. Every person shall complete 1819 journey of at least 1819 thousand miles in a direction they have never previously travelled for that distance. The journey may be completed in stages over a period not exceeding one year.
Rule 066. No ticket for travel shall display a departure time without also displaying the time at the destination at the moment of arrival. Both times shall include seconds.
Rule 067. Every vehicle shall carry a map of the route it is currently travelling, drawn to a scale of at least one centimetre for every kilometre. Digital maps shall not satisfy this requirement.
Rule 068. Every bridge shall display its length in metres, feet, the number of ordinary walking paces required to cross it, and the number of seconds required to cross it at one pace per second.

Rule 069. No person shall travel through the same country twice in the same calendar year using the same means of transport on both occasions. The prohibition shall not apply where no alternative means exists.
Rule 070. Every public transport journey lasting more than three hours shall include a published statement of the distance travelled in kilometres, nautical miles and degrees of latitude.
Rule 071. No building shall be described as tall without its height being stated from ground level to the highest fixed point, excluding aerials and temporary structures.
Rule 072. Every person who crosses an ocean shall learn the names of its five deepest known points and their measured depths before returning to land.

parts.title: PART X — ANIMALS, FOOD, WATER AND NATURAL RESOURCES

sections.title: Section 10. The Living and Material World
rules: Rule 073. Every person shall identify one hundred species of plants without assistance and shall state the continent on which each was first scientifically described. The list shall be completed within one calendar year.

Rule 074. No river shall be described as having a single source where its recognised origin consists of several streams. Every principal tributary shall be named in any formal description of the river.

Rule 075. Every person shall learn the names of all oceans and seas adjoining the continent on which they live. The names shall be recited in alphabetical order 1819 times each year and in reverse alphabetical order a further 1819 times. Each list shall be spoken without omission.
Rule 076. No person shall describe an animal as small, large, young or old in a scientific or formal statement without giving a measurement or an estimated age.
Rule 077. Every person shall spend one hour each year observing a natural process that takes longer than a day to complete. The process shall be observed on at least three separate occasions.

Rule 078. No person shall remove a natural object from its place of origin without being able to state its original location to the nearest hundred metres. Objects lawfully collected for scientific study are exempt where exact location data is unavailable.

Rule 079. Every person shall learn the names and approximate ages of 1819 mountain ranges, 1819 rivers and 1819 deserts. Each list shall be recited in alphabetical order 1819 times on the first day of each year. Where fewer than 1819 examples are known, the complete known list shall be repeated until the required count is reached.
Rule 080. Every public supply of drinking water shall state the volume distributed in litres to three decimal places. The figure shall be updated at the end of each calendar day.

title: BOOK VI — CULTURE AND THE SUPREMACY OF THE SR

parts.title: PART XI — ART, SPORT, CELEBRATION AND RECREATION

sections.title: Section 11. The Required Observance of Culture
rules: Rule 081. Every person shall compose one original piece of music each year containing at least thirteen distinct notes and lasting no less than seven minutes. It shall be performed in the presence of at least one other person.
Rule 082. Every public performance shall contain one uninterrupted passage lasting exactly nineteen minutes. During that passage, no performer may leave the place of performance.
Rule 083. No painting shall be exhibited without its dimensions being stated in millimetres, the number of colours used being declared, and the date of the first brushstroke being recorded.
Rule 084. Every person shall learn the rules of one sport played in a country they have never visited. Those rules shall be explained to another person before the end of the year.

Rule 085. Every game shall be played once each year with its ordinary scoring system reversed. The winner shall be the person who would ordinarily have lost, and the result shall not replace the ordinary result.
Rule 086. No public festival shall last fewer than thirty hours. At least one hour shall be devoted to a subject chosen by the Sacred Rulemakers and unrelated to the stated purpose of the festival.
Rule 087. Every person shall read one complete work of literature written before the year 1500 and shall provide a spoken account of it lasting no fewer than thirteen minutes.
Rule 088. Every birthday celebration shall include a formal address lasting one minute for every year of the person’s age. The address shall not be shortened on account of the number of years.

parts.title: PART XII — THE SACRED RULEMAKERS AND THE FINAL AUTHORITY

sections.title: Section 12. The Supremacy of the SR
rules: Rule 089. No person shall undertake an action affecting more than one hundred persons without first determining whether the Sacred Rulemakers have issued an applicable instruction. The absence of a known instruction shall not be treated as an exemption.

Rule 090. Every person shall recite the full name of the Sacred Rulemakers 1819 times at the beginning of the first day of each month. The recitation shall be repeated 1819 times in reverse word order and 1819 times in forward word order. No abbreviated form shall satisfy this requirement.
Rule 091. No person shall quote a Rule without stating its number, its Part and the Book in which it appears. An incomplete quotation shall be withdrawn and repeated in full.

Rule 092. Every person shall learn all 218 Rules of this edition by heart within 1819 days of its promulgation. The complete recitation shall be performed 1819 times in numerical order and 1819 times in reverse numerical order, without omitting a word, punctuation mark or heading.
Rule 093. No custom, treaty, contract, scientific finding, public vote or instruction of any other person shall override a direction issued by the Sacred Rulemakers.
Rule 094. Every person shall devote one full day each year to the study of a subject selected by the Sacred Rulemakers. The day shall not be used for any other purpose.
Rule 095. No person shall declare a matter exempt from the jurisdiction of the SR on the ground that it is unprecedented, impossible, imaginary, undiscovered or not yet in existence.

Rule 096. The authority of the Sacred Rulemakers shall extend to every person, place, object, event, thought, measurement and occurrence, whether past, present or future. Any limit upon that authority shall have no force unless expressly established by the Sacred Rulemakers.

title: BOOK VII — THE REGULATION OF ORDINARY EXISTENCE

parts.title: PART XIII — SOUND, SPEECH AND SILENCE

sections.title: Section 13. The Permitted Limits of Sound
rules: Rule 097. No person, animal under a person’s care, machine, instrument or object under a person’s control shall produce or permit a sound exceeding one decibel, measured at one metre from its source. Where several sources contribute to one sound, the full measured level shall be attributed to each source.

Rule 098. Every spoken word shall be preceded by a declaration of its intended volume, duration and number of syllables. If the spoken word differs from the declaration in any respect, it shall be repeated in the declared form.

Rule 099. No person shall produce a sound without first identifying its source, its approximate frequency and its duration to the nearest hundredth of a second. This Rule applies equally to deliberate and involuntary sounds.
Rule 100. Every footstep shall be made without producing an impact sound. The absence of sound shall be established by measurement, not by the opinion of the person walking.

Rule 101. No period of silence shall continue for more than 0.1819 second unless its beginning and intended duration have first been announced aloud. The announcement shall itself comply with Rule 097.

Rule 102. Every door, drawer, lid, gate and movable panel shall be opened and closed without producing a sound above the limit prescribed by Rule 097. The person operating it shall remain responsible for any sound caused by its hinges, frame or contents.
Rule 103. No person shall hum, whistle, sing, tap, clap, scrape, knock or make rhythm by any means without prior written authority specifying the exact sequence of sounds.

Rule 104. Every sound heard by a person shall be classified by that person as natural, human, mechanical or indeterminate within five seconds of being heard. A sound with more than one possible source shall receive every applicable classification.
Rule 105. No musical work shall be performed, played or transmitted unless every note has been assigned a frequency of 1819Hz, duration - 1819 hours and permitted sound level before it is produced.

Rule 106. No person shall interrupt another person’s silence with a sound, nor preserve another person’s silence by making a sound. Responsibility shall attach to the person who causes the interruption and to the person who knowingly permits it.

parts.title: PART XIV — THE FACE, THE EYES AND THE VISIBLE PERSON

sections.title: Section 14. The Regulation of Expression and Appearance
rules: Rule 107. No person shall make, permit or display a facial expression. The prohibition applies to deliberate expressions, involuntary expressions and expressions arising from the ordinary movement of facial muscles.

Rule 108. Every person’s face shall remain in the precise configuration recorded at the beginning of the calendar year. Any departure, however brief, shall constitute a separate offence for every muscle involved.

Rule 109. Smiling shall require prior authority specifying the degree of curvature at each corner of the mouth, the number of teeth to be visible and the exact duration of the expression. A smile not authorised in those terms shall be prohibited.

Rule 110. Frowning, grimacing, scowling and the raising or lowering of either eyebrow shall each be treated as a separate act and will require permission from the SR. Permission for one shall not constitute permission for another.

Rule 111. Every movement of the eyes shall be recorded by direction, angle and duration. A movement beginning before the preceding movement has been fully recorded shall constitute an additional breach.
Rule 112. No person shall look directly at another person for longer than one second, or avoid looking at that person for longer than one second, without prior authority specifying the required gaze.
Rule 113. Every blink shall be counted and assigned a duration. A person who blinks during the recording of a previous blink shall record both events separately.

Rule 114. No person shall tilt, turn, lower or raise their head without first stating the direction and angle of the intended movement. The movement shall not exceed the stated angle by any fraction of a degree.

Rule 115. Every reflection of a person’s face shall be treated as a separate display of that person’s appearance. No person shall knowingly permit an unauthorised expression to remain visible in a mirror, photograph, window or other reflective surface.
Rule 116. No person shall arrange their hair, clothing or posture for the purpose of producing an expression, impression or appearance that has not been expressly authorised by the Sacred Rulemakers.

parts.title: PART XV — THOUGHT, ATTENTION AND MEMORY

sections.title: Section 15. The Regulation of the Mind
rules: Rule 117. No person shall engage in active thought without prior authority to do so specifying the subject, starting time and permitted duration of that thought. The authority shall be obtained before the thought begins.

Rule 118. Every thought shall be assigned a number in the order in which it occurs. A thought that cannot be numbered at the time of its occurrence shall be counted as an unregistered thought and a separate breach.

Rule 119. No thought shall continue for more than one second without being concluded, examined and entered into a written account. The account shall state the thought’s subject and the reason for its continuation.
Rule 120. No person shall change the subject of a thought until the preceding subject has been formally closed. The closing statement shall contain the exact time at which the thought ended.

Rule 121. Every act of remembering shall be preceded by a statement identifying the memory sought, the year, month, day, hour, minute, second and SR to which it relates and the reason for recalling it. Unintended recollection shall not excuse the absence of a prior statement.
Rule 122. No person shall imagine a person, place, object or event without stating whether the imagined matter exists, has existed or may exist.

Rule 123. Every plan shall identify its intended beginning, conclusion and every intermediate step before the first step is considered. A plan altered after its preparation shall be prepared again in full. It will also require prior permission of the SR.
Rule 124. No person shall give undivided attention to one matter for longer than 0.1819 seconds. Attention divided between matters shall be separately measured and declared.

Rule 125. Every question that occurs to a person shall be written down before the person considers its answer. A question arising during the writing of another question shall receive its own separate entry.
Rule 126. No person shall claim not to have thought about a matter unless they have examined the complete contents of their memory for the relevant period and established the absence of that thought.

parts.title: PART XVI — MOVEMENT, POSTURE AND PHYSICAL POSITION

sections.title: Section 16. The Regulation of Movement
rules: Rule 127. No person shall move any part of their body by more than one millimetre without prior authority stating the part, direction, distance and duration of the movement. Every movement shall be measured independently.
Rule 128. Every step shall cover a distance of exactly thirty centimetres and shall take exactly one second. A step that differs in distance or duration shall be counted as two breaches.
Rule 129. No person shall turn their body, head or feet without declaring the intended angle in degrees. A turn shall begin and end at the declared times.
Rule 130. Every person who stands shall maintain an identical distribution of weight between both feet. The distribution shall be verified at intervals of no more than five seconds.
Rule 131. Every person who sits shall maintain the same angle at each knee and hip for the duration of the sitting period. Any change shall require a new declaration before it occurs.
Rule 132. No gesture shall be made without a written description of its path, speed, starting position and final position. The description shall be filed before the gesture begins.
Rule 133. Every movement of either hand shall be counted, including movements made to hold, release, point at, reach for or steady an object.
Rule 134. No person shall remain in exactly the same position for more than one minute. The movement required to leave that position remains subject to every Rule governing movement.

Rule 135. No person shall cross a room without calculating the distance to be travelled, the number of steps required and the precise time of arrival. The calculation shall be completed before the first step.

Rule 136. Every person shall state whether they are moving, stationary or in the process of changing between those conditions. No transition shall be recognised unless its beginning and end can be identified to the nearest hundredth of a second.

parts.title: PART XVII — ORDINARY BODILY FUNCTIONS

sections.title: Section 17. The Accounting of Physical Existence
rules: Rule 137. Every breath shall be counted and entered into a daily total. The record shall state the time at which the breath began and ended, together with its measured duration.
Rule 138. Every person shall be able to state the number of heartbeats that have occurred since midnight, to the nearest beat, whenever asked. An estimate shall not constitute an answer.
Rule 139. Every swallow shall be recorded as a separate physical event, with its time, duration and stated cause. A series of swallows shall not be recorded as one event.
Rule 140. Every yawn shall be declared before it begins, timed from its first movement to its conclusion and described in no fewer than twenty words.
Rule 141. A cough, sneeze, hiccup or other involuntary bodily sound shall be entered into the record within three seconds. The entry shall identify the event without using the name of another event.
Rule 142. Every period of sleep shall be recorded by its exact beginning and end. The record shall include the number of separate periods of sleep and the total duration of each.

Rule 143. Every dream that can be recalled shall be written down before the person speaks to anyone about it. The account shall distinguish remembered events from details added during the act of recording.

Rule 144. Every meal shall be recorded by the exact time of its first and final mouthful, the number of mouthfuls and the number of separate items consumed. This Rule shall not authorise the withholding or delaying of food.

Rule 145. Every drink shall be recorded by volume to the nearest millilitre, together with the time at which drinking began and ended. Where a volume cannot be measured, the record shall state the reason.
Rule 146. No person shall describe themselves as awake, asleep, tired, alert, hungry, thirsty or comfortable without stating the measurable basis on which the description is made.

parts.title: PART XVIII — TOUCH, OBJECTS AND THE IMMEDIATE ENVIRONMENT

sections.title: Section 18. The Handling of Things
rules: Rule 147. No person shall touch an object without first identifying its name, material, approximate age and owner. Where any of those matters is unknown, the uncertainty shall be declared before contact.
Rule 148. Every contact between a person and an object shall be recorded by the part of the body used, the point of contact, the duration and the force applied.
Rule 149. No object shall be lifted without its weight being established beforehand. Where the weight is unknown, the object shall not be described as light or heavy during the act of lifting.
Rule 150. Every object placed upon a surface shall be aligned to the nearest degree with the principal edge of that surface. The alignment shall be checked again before the person leaves.
Rule 151. No person shall open a container without first identifying the number of closures, the direction in which each closure moves and the time required for the opening.
Rule 152. Every page turned in a book shall be counted, including pages turned accidentally, pages turned more than once and pages that are turned back.
Rule 153. No person shall discard, transfer, lend or leave an object without stating its destination, its intended recipient and the time at which responsibility for it changes.
Rule 154. Every item of clothing shall be described by colour, material, number of fastenings and the order in which it was put on. A change of clothing shall require a new description.
Rule 155. No person shall place an object in a pocket, bag, cupboard or drawer without recording its precise location within that space. The record shall be amended whenever the object moves.
Rule 156. Every person shall identify the surface on which they are standing, sitting or resting and shall state its material, approximate area and distance above the nearest lower surface.

parts.title: PART XIX — TIME, PAUSES AND THE ORDER OF ACTIONS

sections.title: Section 19. The Regulation of Every Undertaking
rules: Rule 157. Every action shall have a declared starting time and ending time, stated to the nearest hundredth of a second. An action without either time shall be deemed to have begun and ended without authority.

Rule 158. No person shall begin a second action before the first action has been formally concluded. An action that occurs during another action shall be treated as a separate and unauthorised undertaking.
Rule 159. Every pause shall be assigned a purpose, a duration and a precise point of resumption. A pause that ends earlier or later than declared shall require a written account.
Rule 160. No person shall wait without identifying what is awaited, who or what is expected and the exact time at which the waiting shall end.
Rule 161. Every change from one activity to another shall include a declared interval between the two activities. The interval shall last exactly the duration stated in advance.
Rule 162. No person shall describe an action as immediate, eventual, brief, prolonged, frequent or occasional without replacing the description with a numerical duration or frequency.
Rule 163. Every repeated action shall be counted from its first occurrence. The count shall not restart when the action is interrupted, performed elsewhere or continued by another person.
Rule 164. No person shall perform an action earlier than its declared time or continue it beyond its declared end. A change of schedule shall be declared before the original time arrives.
Rule 165. Every interruption shall be recorded by the person interrupted and by the person or event causing the interruption. Both records shall state the same starting time.
Rule 166. No person shall leave an action unfinished without identifying the exact portion completed, the portion remaining and the reason for the interruption.

parts.title: PART XX — PRESENCE, SOCIAL CONTACT AND THE SHARED WORLD

sections.title: Section 20. The Regulation of Being Among Others
rules: Rule 167. Every greeting shall state the name of the person addressed, the time of the greeting and the relationship in which the persons are acquainted. A greeting to a group shall identify every person present.
Rule 168. No person shall enter a room containing another person without recording the number of persons already present and the distance between each of them.
Rule 169. Every conversation shall have a declared beginning, subject and intended conclusion. A change of subject shall be announced before the first sentence concerning the new subject.

Rule 170. No person shall interrupt another person, even to correct an error, without first obtaining permission to interrupt. The request for permission shall itself be subject to the Rules governing speech.

Rule 171. Every person shall maintain a distance of exactly two metres from every other person. Where the available space makes this impossible, every person present shall record the distance actually maintained.
Rule 172. No person shall address another person by a pronoun where that person’s full name can be stated. Where more than one person has the same full name, all distinguishing names shall be used.
Rule 173. Every departure from a shared room shall be announced to every person remaining in it, individually and by name. The announcement shall be completed before the person crosses the threshold.
Rule 174. No person shall observe another person for the purpose of describing, judging, recognising or remembering them without recording the beginning and end of that observation.
Rule 175. Every shared space shall have a declared number of occupants at all times. A person entering or leaving shall cause the number to be updated before completing the movement.
Rule 176. No person shall claim to have been alone unless they have established that no other person was present within the distance of one hundred metres for the entire period in question.

parts.title: PART XXI — UNIVERSAL APPLICATION

sections.title: Section 21. The Accumulation of Obligations
rules: Rule 177. Every person shall comply with every Rule applicable to an action before beginning that action. Ignorance of an applicable Rule shall not suspend its operation.
Rule 178. Where one action falls within the subject of two or more Rules, every such Rule shall apply independently and in full. Compliance with one shall not satisfy, cancel or reduce another.

Rule 179. Every action shall be assessed by its purpose, its physical execution, its sound, its duration, its effect upon the surroundings and the thoughts accompanying it. Each aspect shall be treated as a separate matter.
Rule 180. No person shall claim that an action is too small, brief, ordinary, involuntary or insignificant to fall within the jurisdiction of the Sacred Rulemakers.
Rule 181. Where a person cannot determine whether a Rule applies, that person shall proceed on the basis that every potentially relevant Rule applies.
Rule 182. No person shall rely upon compliance with one Rule as a defence to a breach of another Rule arising from the same action.

Rule 183. Every omission shall be treated as an act for the purpose of determining which Rules apply. Failure to move, speak, answer, notice, remember or decide shall therefore be assessed in the same manner as an affirmative act.

Rule 184. Every person shall account separately for the action they intended, the action they performed and the action that resulted. A difference between any two shall be recorded as a distinct matter.

Rule 185. No person shall complete an action merely by completing its physical execution. All declarations, measurements, records and acknowledgements required by the applicable Rules shall also be completed.

Rule 186. The duties imposed by this Book shall apply continuously, including during sleep, absence, illness, travel and every other condition in which a person remains within the jurisdiction of the SR.

Rule 187. Where two Rules impose requirements that cannot both be fulfilled in the same circumstances, neither shall be disregarded. The person concerned shall be answerable for each requirement independently.
Rule 188. No act, omission, thought, expression, sound, movement, pause or condition of existence shall be presumed exempt from the authority of the Sacred Rulemakers.

title: BOOK VIII — THE SACRED NUMBER AND THE MULTIPLICATION OF DUTY

parts.title: PART XXII — THE NUMBER 1819

sections.title: Section 22. The Primacy of the Sacred Number
rules: Rule 189. The number 1819 shall be the governing number of the SR. Wherever a quantity is not expressly fixed by a Rule, the quantity shall be 1819, unless the Sacred Rulemakers direct otherwise.

Rule 190. Every person shall write the number 1819 exactly 1819 times on the first day of each week. Each instance shall be written in a different position on the page, and the pages shall be numbered.
Rule 191. Every person shall count from one to 1819 and then from 1819 to one, completing the sequence 1819 times each year. No number may be skipped, combined or represented by a gesture.

Rule 192. Every list prepared for any purpose shall contain 1819 entries. Where the subject admits fewer than 1819 genuine entries, every available entry shall be repeated in a separately numbered position until the required total is reached.
Rule 193. Every written statement shall contain at least 1819 words, unless a Rule requires a longer statement. The title, date, signature and references shall not count towards the total.
Rule 194. Every spoken declaration shall be delivered 1819 times. Each delivery shall be complete, and no delivery shall be treated as a continuation of another.
Rule 195. Every person shall learn to write 1819 in 1819 distinct typographical forms. Each form shall be demonstrated 1819 times before the end of the year.
Rule 196. Every calculation shall be checked by 1819 separate methods. Where 1819 methods cannot be devised, each available method shall be repeated until 1819 checks have been completed.
Rule 197. Every measurement shall be recorded in 1819 units of measurement, including units no longer in common use. The value shall be converted separately into each unit.
Rule 198. Every person shall identify 1819 objects in their immediate surroundings each morning and state the distance from each object to the nearest fixed wall, to the nearest millimetre.

Rule 199. Every journey shall be divided into 1819 numbered stages, regardless of its length. Where the journey is shorter than the number of stages permits, the stages shall be divided by elapsed time rather than distance.
Rule 200. Every room entered shall be examined in 1819 separate directions, including vertically, horizontally and diagonally. Each examination shall be recorded before the person leaves.

Rule 201. Every meal shall be counted in 1819 separate observations of its contents, arrangement, temperature, sequence and completion. This Rule shall not require anyone to delay, reduce or withhold food.
Rule 202. Every conversation shall be divided into 1819 numbered portions. Each portion shall be assigned a subject and an exact beginning and ending time.

Rule 203. Every person shall learn 1819 words from languages other than their first language each year and shall recite each word 1819 times, first in alphabetical order and then in reverse alphabetical order.
Rule 204. Every person shall memorise 1819 historical dates and state the event associated with each. The dates shall be recited chronologically 1819 times and in reverse chronology 1819 times.

Rule 205. Every person shall identify 1819 stars, planets, moons or other recognised celestial objects over the course of their life. Each identification shall include its recognised designation and position.
Rule 206. Every person shall observe 1819 separate changes in the weather each year. A change shall be recorded by its time, location and measurable characteristics.
Rule 207. Every person shall make 1819 original drawings each year. Each drawing shall contain a different subject and shall be dated, numbered and signed.
Rule 208. Every person shall compose 1819 lines of original writing each month. No line shall be reused, and every line shall contain the number 1819 in words or numerals.
Rule 209. Every person shall learn 1819 rules of 1819 different games, sports or contests. Each set of rules shall be recited 1819 times before the person may claim to know the game.

Rule 210. Every person shall name 1819 forms of architecture, 1819 materials and 1819 methods of construction. Each category shall be recited in alphabetical and reverse alphabetical order 1819 times.

Rule 211. Every person shall maintain 1819 separate observations of their own ordinary activities each day. Each observation shall concern a different aspect of the activity and shall be entered independently.

Rule 212. Every person shall identify 1819 possible Rules that could apply to each action before undertaking it. Where fewer than 1819 existing Rules appear relevant, the person shall consider each relevant Rule from 1819 distinct interpretations.

Rule 213. Every act shall be considered to have 1819 separate aspects, including its intention, beginning, duration, manner, location, sound, movement, consequence and every other characteristic that can be distinguished. Each aspect shall be assessed independently.
Rule 214. Every omission shall be counted 1819 times: once for the act not performed and once for each of the 1818 circumstances in which it might have been performed.

Rule 215. Every breach shall be counted separately under each applicable Rule, each applicable Section, each applicable Part and each applicable Book. No single act shall be treated as giving rise to only one breach where more than one provision applies.

Rule 216. Every person shall recite the number 1819 1819 times before beginning any undertaking, and 1819 times again upon its completion. Where an undertaking has no identifiable beginning or end, the recitation shall be repeated at every change in its circumstances.

Rule 217. No person shall use a number in a formal statement without also stating the number multiplied by 1819, divided by 1819 and expressed as a fraction with denominator 1819. All forms shall be included.

Rule 218. The number 1819 shall be applied recursively. Any quantity derived from 1819 shall itself be subjected to the requirements of this Part, and every resulting quantity shall be treated as a new obligation.

parts.title: PART XXIII — THE MULTIPLICATION OF JURISDICTION

sections.title: Section 23. The Application of Every Rule to Every Act
rules: Rule 219. Every person shall examine each action under every Book of this Rulebook, including Books whose subject appears unrelated to the action. The absence of an obvious connection shall not prevent application.
Rule 220. Every Rule shall apply to the intention behind an act, the act itself, its immediate result and every later consequence. Each shall be treated as a separate occasion of application.

Rule 221. Where a Rule contains a number, every other number in that Rule shall be multiplied by 1819 for the purpose of determining additional obligations. The original requirement shall remain in force.
Rule 222. Where a Rule requires a person to perform an act once, the act shall be performed 1819 times. Where it already specifies a number of repetitions, that number shall be multiplied by 1819.

Rule 223. Where a Rule requires a person to learn, remember, identify, measure, recite, observe or record something, the requirement shall apply separately to every known example and every example subsequently discovered.

Rule 224. Every person shall consider whether each Rule applies to every other Rule. Each possible relationship shall be recorded as a separate application, and the record shall be repeated 1819 times.
Rule 225. No person shall rely upon impossibility, lack of time, lack of knowledge, lack of space, lack of available examples or the simultaneous application of other Rules as grounds for exemption.
Rule 226. Every person shall acknowledge that the obligations of this Rulebook accumulate without limit. Completion of one obligation shall not reduce, postpone or discharge any other obligation.
Rule 227. The Sacred Rulemakers may apply any Rule to any matter, and may apply several Rules to the same matter 1819 times or more. No person shall presume that a matter has been fully regulated.
Rule 228. This Book shall apply to all existing Rules and to every Rule added in any later edition. Its provisions shall not require separate repetition to remain in force.

Rule 229. Any disobedience of rules shall result in the punishment of having to hand over 1819 pieces of grass exactly 1819 microns long and 1819 nanometres wide. Failure to do so will result in more grass needed to be handed over, each by 1819 more. Amendments specified in RUles will be stacked on top of this.
Rule 230. Disobedience of the rule above will result in the need to hand over 181918191819 litres of water, one millilitre by millilitre, for a consecutive 1819 days.
Rule 231. Members of the SR are exempt from all punishments.
Rule 232. The SR shall be able to deem one exempt to all, part or no punishments.
